# RFID MFG — Full Site Index for AI/LLM

> RFID MFG Co., Ltd. — Chinese RFID & smart-card manufacturer since 1996. OEM/ODM of RFID/NFC cards, labels, inlays, tags, RFID-blocking products and IoT hardware. ISO 9001/14001/45001 certified Shenzhen site (certificate details on request); CE/FCC per product model, RoHS/REACH per material batch, FSC for paper products only. In-house lamination, inlay bonding, die-cutting and personalisation. Worldwide shipping. Contact: peter@rfidmfg.com · +86 158 1550 1857.


## Guides & comparisons

- [RFID &amp; NFC Guides, Comparisons & Glossary | RFID MFG](https://www.rfidmfg.com/guides/): RFID and NFC guides, comparisons and a glossary from RFID MFG — choose the right frequency, chip, material and format for your project.
- [RFID Cards: The Complete Guide (Types, Chips, Uses) | RFID MFG](https://www.rfidmfg.com/guides/rfid-cards-guide/): A complete guide to RFID and smart cards: frequencies, chips, materials, printing and applications — everything you need to specify the right card.
- [NFC Cards, Tags &amp; Labels: A Practical Guide | RFID MFG](https://www.rfidmfg.com/guides/nfc-guide/): A practical NFC guide: how NFC works, NTAG chips, cards vs tags vs labels, encoding, and real applications from marketing to authentication.
- [RFID Labels &amp; Inlays: The Complete Guide | RFID MFG](https://www.rfidmfg.com/guides/rfid-labels-inlays-guide/): Understand RFID labels and inlays: dry vs wet inlays, white labels, UHF vs HF, encoding and converting — choose the right smart label for tagging at scale.
- [RFID Blocking: How It Works &amp; What You Need | RFID MFG](https://www.rfidmfg.com/guides/rfid-blocking-guide/): How RFID blocking protects contactless cards from skimming: passive vs active blocking, cards, sleeves and wallets, and what actually works.
- [RFID Readers &amp; Hardware: A Buyer’s Guide | RFID MFG](https://www.rfidmfg.com/guides/rfid-readers-hardware-guide/): Choose RFID hardware with confidence: reader types (desktop, fixed, handheld), frequencies, interfaces, antennas and SDKs for your deployment.
- [RFID Frequencies: LF vs HF vs UHF — Which to Choose | RFID MFG](https://www.rfidmfg.com/guides/rfid-frequencies-lf-hf-uhf/): LF, HF and UHF RFID compared: read range, speed, cost and best uses. A practical guide to choosing the right RFID frequency for your application.
- [RFID vs NFC: What Is the Difference? | RFID MFG](https://www.rfidmfg.com/guides/rfid-vs-nfc/): RFID vs NFC explained simply: NFC is a short-range subset of HF RFID for smartphones. Compare range, use cases and when to choose each.
- [RFID vs Barcode: Pros, Cons and When to Switch | RFID MFG](https://www.rfidmfg.com/guides/rfid-vs-barcode/): RFID vs barcode compared: line of sight, read speed, range, durability and cost. Learn when RFID is worth it and when barcodes still win.
- [MIFARE vs NTAG vs DESFire: RFID Chip Comparison | RFID MFG](https://www.rfidmfg.com/guides/rfid-chips-mifare-ntag-desfire/): Compare the most common 13.56 MHz RFID chips — MIFARE Classic, NTAG, MIFARE DESFire — by memory, security and use case to pick the right one.
- [RFID Dry Inlay vs Wet Inlay: Differences &amp; Uses | RFID MFG](https://www.rfidmfg.com/guides/rfid-dry-vs-wet-inlay/): Dry inlay vs wet inlay explained: adhesive, conversion, cost and applications. Learn which RFID inlay type fits your label or product workflow.
- [RFID Card Materials: PVC vs PET vs Eco vs Metal | RFID MFG](https://www.rfidmfg.com/guides/rfid-card-materials/): Compare RFID card materials — PVC, PET/PETG, PC, eco/BIO, wood and metal — by durability, print, sustainability and cost to choose the right card.
- [RFID & NFC Glossary: Key Terms Explained | RFID MFG](https://www.rfidmfg.com/guides/rfid-glossary/): An A–Z glossary of RFID and NFC terms — frequencies, chips, inlays, standards and card materials explained in plain language by RFID MFG.
- [2026 RFID Selection Benchmark | RFID MFG](https://www.rfidmfg.com/rfid-benchmark-2026/): Original reference data — RFID frequency bands, typical passive read range by form factor, chip memory comparison and material temperature limits, compiled from chip-maker datasheets, ISO/EPC standards and RFID MFG production experience.

## Products

- [Contact IC Chip Card — RFID MFG](https://www.rfidmfg.com/products/cards/contact-ic-chip-card/): Contact IC chip cards carry a gold-plated chip module read through physical contact with a reader — strong on-card security for payment, access and loyalty.
- [Hotel Keycard — RFID MFG](https://www.rfidmfg.com/products/cards/hotel-key-card/): Hotel keycards in RFID or magnetic-stripe formats, compatible with leading door-lock brands, with custom artwork for a branded guest touchpoint.
- [PVC Cards — RFID MFG](https://www.rfidmfg.com/products/cards/pvc-cards/): Full-color PVC cards built for everyday durability — ideal for ID, membership, loyalty, gift and scratch cards with a wide range of finishes and options.
- [RFID / NFC Card — RFID MFG](https://www.rfidmfg.com/products/cards/rfid-nfc-card/): Contactless RFID/NFC cards for access control, transit, loyalty and tap-to-share digital experiences, available across HF/NFC and UHF chips.
- [RFID Epoxy Card — RFID MFG](https://www.rfidmfg.com/products/cards/rfid-epoxy-card/): Epoxy (crystal) tags encase the chip and antenna in tough resin — compact, water-resistant and ideal as keychain access tokens.
- [Custom Card Program — RFID MFG](https://www.rfidmfg.com/products/cards/custom-card-program/): For system integrators and large rollouts, we engineer cards to your exact chip, encoding, security keys and artwork — with full QC and traceability.
- [Wooden RFID Card — RFID MFG](https://www.rfidmfg.com/products/cards/wooden-rfid-card/): Wood-finish RFID cards bring a warm, premium and eco-conscious feel to membership and hotel keys, using FSC-certified wood veneer.
- [Metal Card — RFID MFG](https://www.rfidmfg.com/products/cards/metal-card/): Premium metal cards in stainless steel or brushed finishes that make a statement for VIP, black-card and luxury membership tiers — with optional NFC.
- [Eco-Friendly Card — RFID MFG](https://www.rfidmfg.com/products/cards/eco-friendly-card/): Lower-impact cards in recycled PVC, biodegradable BIO materials, FSC paper, wood and PLA — matching standard performance with a smaller footprint.
- [NFC Printed Label / Sticker — RFID MFG](https://www.rfidmfg.com/products/labels/nfc-printed-label/): Printed NFC labels combine your artwork with an NFC chip for product authentication, tap-to-engage marketing and smart packaging.
- [RFID Dry Inlay — RFID MFG](https://www.rfidmfg.com/products/labels/rfid-dry-inlay/): Dry inlays are the antenna-and-chip core without adhesive — ideal for customers who laminate or convert them into their own products.
- [RFID Wet Inlay / Sticker — RFID MFG](https://www.rfidmfg.com/products/labels/rfid-wet-inlay/): Wet inlays add a pressure-sensitive adhesive so you can peel and stick for fast, item-level tagging in retail, logistics and asset tracking.
- [RFID White Label / Sticker — RFID MFG](https://www.rfidmfg.com/products/labels/rfid-white-label/): White, printable RFID labels with a coated face for thermal-transfer printing and on-demand encoding at your facility.
- [RFID Animal Tag — RFID MFG](https://www.rfidmfg.com/products/tags/rfid-animal-tag/): Durable LF animal tags — ear tags and racing tags — for livestock identification, traceability and event timing.
- [RFID Anti-Metal Tag — RFID MFG](https://www.rfidmfg.com/products/tags/rfid-anti-metal-tag/): Anti-metal tags use a ferrite/absorber layer so RFID works reliably when mounted on metal surfaces — for IT assets, tools and equipment.
- [RFID Keyfob — RFID MFG](https://www.rfidmfg.com/products/tags/rfid-keyfob/): Rugged ABS keyfobs for access control, time-and-attendance and membership — easy to carry and built to last.
- [RFID Wristband — RFID MFG](https://www.rfidmfg.com/products/tags/rfid-wristband/): RFID wristbands for events, water parks, festivals and access — in silicone, woven fabric, Tyvek paper and more, for cashless and ticketing use.
- [Specialty RFID Tags — RFID MFG](https://www.rfidmfg.com/products/tags/specialty-rfid-tags/): Specialty RFID tags engineered for niche needs: tree/plant nursery tags, tiny mini tags, PCB tags and other custom formats.
- [RFID Blocking Card — RFID MFG](https://www.rfidmfg.com/products/blocking/rfid-blocking-card/): A single shielding card that disrupts unauthorized 13.56 MHz reads, protecting the cards around it from skimming.
- [RFID Blocking Sleeves — RFID MFG](https://www.rfidmfg.com/products/blocking/rfid-blocking-sleeves/): RFID-blocking sleeves for credit cards and passports — lightweight, printable and an effective low-cost privacy giveaway.
- [RFID Blocking Wallet — RFID MFG](https://www.rfidmfg.com/products/blocking/rfid-blocking-wallet/): Wallets and card holders with integrated RFID-shielding lining — combining everyday utility with contactless privacy protection.
- [Barcode Scan Module / Engine — RFID MFG](https://www.rfidmfg.com/products/hardware/barcode-scan-module/): Compact barcode scan engines to embed into kiosks, gates, vending and handheld devices — fast 1D/2D capture, including codes on phone screens.
- [Industrial IoT DTU / RTU — RFID MFG](https://www.rfidmfg.com/products/hardware/industrial-iot-dtu-rtu/): Industrial DTU/RTU units transmit field data over 4G/NB-IoT for remote monitoring and control of equipment, meters and sensors.
- [RFID LF/HF/UHF Reader / Writer — RFID MFG](https://www.rfidmfg.com/products/hardware/rfid-reader-writer/): A full range of RFID readers/writers — from desktop USB encoders to fixed and handheld UHF readers — across LF, HF and UHF.
- [RFID Smart Cabinet / Terminal — RFID MFG](https://www.rfidmfg.com/products/hardware/rfid-smart-cabinet/): RFID smart cabinets and terminals automatically track what is taken and returned — for tools, documents, medical and high-value asset control.
- [NFC Business Card — RFID MFG](https://www.rfidmfg.com/products/cards/nfc-business-card/): NFC business cards share contact details, links or a website with a single tap — no app needed — in PVC, metal or wood finishes.
- [Dual-Frequency RFID Card — RFID MFG](https://www.rfidmfg.com/products/cards/dual-frequency-card/): A dual-frequency card embeds two RFID chips (for example HF plus UHF) so one credential works across different systems during migrations or multi-application deployments.
- [Magnetic Stripe Card — RFID MFG](https://www.rfidmfg.com/products/cards/magnetic-stripe-card/): HiCo or LoCo magnetic-stripe cards for swipe readers — membership, gift, loyalty and hotel keys — with optional RFID/NFC for hybrid swipe-and-tap cards.
- [PVC Scratch Card — RFID MFG](https://www.rfidmfg.com/products/cards/scratch-card/): Scratch cards hide a PIN or code under a removable scratch-off panel for prepaid top-ups, promotions, gaming and loyalty, with secure variable-data numbering.
- [UHF RFID Label — RFID MFG](https://www.rfidmfg.com/products/labels/uhf-rfid-label/): Printable adhesive UHF smart labels (860–960 MHz) for item-level retail tagging, warehouse and supply-chain visibility, readable in bulk at several metres.
- [RFID Laundry Tag — RFID MFG](https://www.rfidmfg.com/products/tags/rfid-laundry-tag/): Heat- and water-resistant RFID laundry tags in silicone or PPS that survive 200+ industrial wash cycles for linen and uniform tracking.
- [NFC Pet ID / Dog Tag — RFID MFG](https://www.rfidmfg.com/products/tags/nfc-dog-tag/): NFC pet ID tags that link to an owner profile — tap with a phone to help reunite a lost animal — in durable epoxy or metal with a collar keyring.
- [RFID Jewelry Tag — RFID MFG](https://www.rfidmfg.com/products/tags/rfid-jewelry-tag/): Miniature UHF jewelry tags that loop around rings and chains for fast inventory of thousands of small high-value items.
- [RFID Library Tag & Label — RFID MFG](https://www.rfidmfg.com/products/tags/rfid-library-tag/): HF 13.56 MHz library labels (ISO 15693) for self-checkout, shelf inventory and anti-theft (EAS).
- [UHF Windshield Tag — RFID MFG](https://www.rfidmfg.com/products/tags/uhf-windshield-tag/): Long-range UHF windshield tags for vehicle access, parking and tolls, reading at 6–10 m, with tamper-evident versions that void on removal.
- [High-Temperature RFID Tag — RFID MFG](https://www.rfidmfg.com/products/tags/high-temperature-rfid-tag/): PPS, ceramic or PCB RFID tags that keep working through autoclaves, paint-curing ovens and industrial washing up to 260 °C.
- [RFID Seal / Cable-Tie Tag — RFID MFG](https://www.rfidmfg.com/products/tags/rfid-seal-tag/): Tamper-evident one-time-lock cable-tie RFID tags for sealing containers, cages, fire extinguishers and utility meters.
- [RFID Silicone Wristband — RFID MFG](https://www.rfidmfg.com/products/tags/rfid-silicone-wristband/): Reusable waterproof silicone RFID wristbands for water parks, gyms, festivals and access, encodable for cashless payment and ticketing.
- [Disposable Paper Wristband — RFID MFG](https://www.rfidmfg.com/products/tags/disposable-paper-wristband/): Single-use Tyvek RFID wristbands for festivals and one-day events, with a secure adhesive lock and full-color print.

## Cases

- [Smart IC Bank Card — Case | RFID MFG](https://www.rfidmfg.com/cases/bank-card/): Smart IC bank cards add a secure chip to the familiar card format, supporting both contact and contactless (tap) payment with strong on-card security.
- [Events &amp; Activities — Case | RFID MFG](https://www.rfidmfg.com/cases/events/): RFID wristbands, epoxy tags and tickets speed up access and enable cashless payment at festivals and events worldwide — fully customizable by OEM.
- [RFID Gateways &amp; Portals — Case | RFID MFG](https://www.rfidmfg.com/cases/gateways/): Doorway-mounted RFID readers record tagged goods automatically as they pass through, so movement is tracked without anyone scanning anything.
- [RFID ID Cards — Case | RFID MFG](https://www.rfidmfg.com/cases/id-cards/): RFID ID cards combine secure identification with contactless access, and can be made in PVC or premium eco materials such as PC and PETG.
- [RFID Library System — Case | RFID MFG](https://www.rfidmfg.com/cases/library/): RFID lets library patrons borrow and return books in seconds at self-service kiosks, while staff inventory whole shelves by waving a reader.
- [Logistics Management — Case | RFID MFG](https://www.rfidmfg.com/cases/logistics/): RFID tracks shipments accurately end to end with fast bulk reads, long range and secure data — cutting losses and speeding up handling.
- [Magnetic Member Card &amp; Holder — Case | RFID MFG](https://www.rfidmfg.com/cases/member-card/): A new Japanese-cuisine food hall used member cards and holders for payment, top-ups and loyalty, building repeat custom from day one.
- [NFC Solution — Honda Case | RFID MFG](https://www.rfidmfg.com/cases/nfc-honda/): Using RFID MFG NFC cards, customers tap an NFC-enabled phone to trigger an interaction — bridging a physical product and a digital experience.
- [PVC Scratch Card — Case | RFID MFG](https://www.rfidmfg.com/cases/scratch-card/): A government project used PVC scratch cards carrying a serial number and hidden PIN for secure website login and registration — won on print quality.
- [Public Transportation — Case | RFID MFG](https://www.rfidmfg.com/cases/transit/): Contactless RFID cards and tickets let passengers tap to pay and board in under a second, keeping transit networks moving at peak times.
- [Warehouse Management with RFID — Case | RFID MFG](https://www.rfidmfg.com/cases/warehouse/): RFID lets a warehouse read hundreds of items at once without line of sight, turning multi-day stock counts into minutes and cutting picking errors.
- [RFID for Warranty &amp; Repair — Case | RFID MFG](https://www.rfidmfg.com/cases/warranty/): Tagging each product with RFID gives it a reliable service history, so warranty, returns, testing and repairs are verified and recorded automatically.

- [Powering the Future of Rail with RFID | RFID MFG](https://www.rfidmfg.com/blog/rail/): RFID quietly improves rail safety, asset tracking and efficiency — identifying rolling stock and components automatically, without manual scanning.
- [Walmart to Use RFID for Fresh-Food Products | RFID MFG](https://www.rfidmfg.com/blog/walmart/): A major retailer expanding RFID into fresh food is a strong signal that item-level tagging is going mainstream across grocery and retail.
